Checkout Redesign

Draft v2

Owner: Payments Platform · Last updated: 2026-10-01

  1. Overview

1. Overview

P0

The current checkout takes 4 steps and loses ~23% of users between Shipping and Payment. This spec collapses checkout into a single page with progressive disclosure, and moves card tokenization to the client using Stripe.js v3.

Note: the “Express Pay” buttons (Apple Pay, Google Pay) are out of scope for v1 — see Rollout.

Success metric: checkout conversion ≥ 78% (baseline 71.4%), measured over 14 days.
Guardrail: payment error rate must stay < 0.5%.

2. Payment flow

Web uses the PaymentElement with layout: "accordion". Address autocomplete is provided by the Places API.

iOS uses PaymentSheet with the FlowController API so we keep our own Confirm button.

Android mirrors iOS via PaymentSheet.FlowController; minimum SDK 24.

Why not keep the multi-step flow?

User research (n=12) showed that the step indicator created “false progress”: users expected to be done after step 3.

3. API changes

EndpointMethodChangeOwner
/v2/checkout/sessionsPOSTNew: creates a session with cart snapshotPayments
PATCHNew: updates shipping address & recalculates tax
/v2/checkout/sessions/{id}/confirmPOSTIdempotent via Idempotency-Key header
/v1/cart/checkoutPOSTDeprecated — returns 410 Gone after 2027-01-01

{
  "cart_id": "crt_8f2a",

}

4. Rollout

  • Week 1: internal dogfood behind checkout_v2 flag
  • Week 2–3: 5% → 25% → 50% A/B
  • Week 4: 100%, remove legacy flow in the following sprint
